text:
Taylor Hall played his 1,000th NHL game this month, at the Global Series in Finland, a long way from being the first overall pick in Edmonton in 2010. The 35-year-old won the Cup with Carolina last spring and a Hart Trophy in 2018, and he is still doing useful things in a smaller role.

He's playing about 13 minutes a night, and in those minutes the Hurricanes own the puck: 67% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, nine points better than without him. His own chances are up to 1.32 expected goals per 60, and he has 7 points in 13 games, right on last season's pace per 60 minutes. Carolina has scored nearly four fewer goals than expected with him out there, so the line's finishing has room to come up.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a playmaker last season, 92nd percentile among forwards in primary shot assists. He missed about three weeks between mid-October and early November, and he dropped the gloves on Nov. 19, only the third fight of his career. Watch his minutes; the impact per shift is there.
headline: Taylor Hall at 1,000 games, still tilting the ice
